dissent: If run_controls is wired to control-build's own inspect_cases, finding 2 is an internal-consistency issue plus an unverified schema assumption rather than a cross-artifact defect; 'patch' may be the exact trace_event key, but batch-07 identity/trace_event source is absent from the packet.
findings: Fresh-capture attestation semantics are decision-insensitive in both files. Implement attest() (~lines 195-215) rejects only 'no-captured-source'/'stale-collection' verdicts, and control-build _frag (~lines 66-72) forbids the same pair, yet originals emit exactly ok|incomplete-inventory|incomplete-registry on a fresh capture (s_inclusive.py:63-69, s_audit.py:89-100); a forged 'source-attest:x' verdict passes undetected. Implement also accepts post['attestation']==(cap[0],cap[1],cut) regardless of decision, so a refused attestation carrying a well-formed commit evades 'attest-commit'; the no-capture branch checks no attestation at all; the ok-without-commit check runs only for side=='source' though the adapter commits identically on Q acceptance (guard_audit.py:76-78; a_inclusive.py:17-18). Fixture: adapter journal event at an attested prefix with decision 'source-attest:incomplete-registry' and journal attestation set to the capture triple yields no mismatch. Fix: closed verdict set; post==pre whenever decision!='source-attest:ok' (all branches, both sides); post==(cap[0],cap[1],cut) when ok.

Control-build reconstruction is not bound to the typed case schema the checker uses. _post (~lines 40-45) takes the first dict-valued member among KEYS, with 'fields' preceding 'state'; real events come from t.trace_event (batch-07; prestage notes patches plus full-state hashes). Multiple dict members or a partial journal patch fabricate keep/write violations on clean evidence or drop fields, and _mut (~lines 99-110) counts hits on heuristic locations that need not affect c.t.restore in the implement checker, so run_controls detections measure a different reconstruction than the shipped checker's. Real interoperability unverified. Fix: restore and mutate through c.t.restore/c.artifact.encode and re-inspect with the shipping inspect_cases.

run_controls _find (~lines 118-125) runs _states over every case and evaluates its predicate at every prefix for each of 13 controls with no charge.take, contradicting the documented accounting (charge.take(1) before each inspected prefix; every repetition counts) and the wave04 explicit-budget requirement. Fix: one reconstruction per case reused across controls and charge per evaluated prefix.

Implement inspect_cases (~lines 230-260) can return 'supported' while cases failed restore or cardinality checks (only listed in limitations), contradicting its docstring 'unproved for ... uninspectable input'. Also, a truthy collection of length<2 reaches cap[1] indexing in attest(), raising IndexError that aborts the whole inspection instead of yielding 'counterexample' (control-build handles len(c)<2). Fix: force 'unproved' on any uninspectable case; treat malformed capture as a boundary violation before indexing.
limitations: Static review only; nothing executed. batch-07 trace_event/restore and q_domain sources are not in the packet, so the real event schema behind _post/_mut is unverified; findings 2 and 3 are contingent on that shape.
'adapter_observation' row key is assumed correct based on boundary.py usage.
No acceptance or execution authorization is asserted; bounded source-review transport gate only.
